briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 5, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis Warning Signs and Immediate Impacts
sections.content: Globally, the warning signs of the climate crisis are becoming increasingly clear. Glaciers in the Swiss Alps have shrunk by 5.5% this year alone [4], and Europe has reported experiencing extreme heatwaves in 2026, following a similar event in 2003 [7]. Domestically, the water level of Cheongdo Unmun Dam has reached a 'severe' stage, escalating concerns about disruptions to tap water supply [36]. Furthermore, Australia recorded its second-hottest September on record due to a combination of El Niño and the climate crisis [83], and a large-scale methane leak has been discovered in Türkiye, the host country for the UN Climate Summit, adding to the severity [86]. Beyond these extreme weather phenomena, socio-economic issues such as reduced crop yields after the installation of agri-voltaic solar panels [1], exploitation of food industry workers [51], and an increase in child marriage and teenage pregnancies are also being identified as impacts of climate change [58, 61, 76].

sections.title: 🌍 Deepening Discussions on Global Climate Action and Legal Responsibility
sections.content: As the international community discusses strengthening global climate action ahead of COP31 [2], legal battles over responsibility for climate change are simultaneously intensifying. The U.S. Supreme Court has begun its new term with major climate change cases [37, 38, 41, 45, 46, 48, 60, 72], and is hearing attempts by states to block climate damage lawsuits filed against major energy companies [53, 81]. During this process, it was noted that the arguments made by oil companies were 'vague' [59]. These legal disputes raise fundamental questions about who will bear the costs of climate change [55, 70], and actor Paul Rudd also warned that 'time is definitely running out' regarding climate change [71]. Meanwhile, while the UK is expected to place climate issues on the international agenda as the G20 chair [85], claims that the Conservative Party's plan to relax energy efficiency regulations will incur an additional £1,000 per year for new homeowners [80], and warnings about the UK government's complacent approach to food security [84], underscore the importance of policy consistency. A report indicating low participation from non-Pacific leaders at the Pre-Cop meeting [82] suggests difficulties in international cooperation.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Efforts for Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Expansion
sections.content: Both domestically and internationally, efforts to achieve carbon neutrality and expand renewable energy are active. In Busan's Oncheoncheon, carbon-neutral initiatives continued on Gaecheonjeol (National Foundation Day) [9, 21], and the Incheon Environmental Corporation encouraged citizen participation through its 'Resource Circulation and Carbon Neutrality Camping with Dad' program [10, 11, 12, 13, 22]. Gwachon City's final report meeting for its local energy plan [14] and Gwangmyeong City's citizen climate tour [15] demonstrate concrete carbon neutrality plans and expanded citizen participation by local governments. Notably, Daegu City secured new carbon credits amounting to 219,000 tons through landfill gas valorization [19, 23], showing tangible reduction achievements, and Cheonan City also actively promoted carbon neutrality practices [20]. In the renewable energy sector, while the importance of public participation is emphasized [24, 33], Jeonnam Development Corporation and Korea Western Power are collaborating to expand renewable energy and activate onshore wind power in the Honam region [32, 35], and various attempts for future energy transition are continuing, such as the commencement of clean hydrogen production technology development using renewable energy [27, 29, 31].

sections.title: 🌱 Strengthening Resilience Through Climate Adaptation and Education
sections.content: Adaptation strategies and efforts to strengthen citizen capabilities in response to the impacts of climate change are also steadily continuing. In Gyeongsangbuk-do, on-site evaluations of over 120 preliminary new rice varieties adapted to climate change are underway [3], and Gongju City in Chungnam is striving to raise awareness by holding special lectures to enhance citizens' capabilities in responding to the climate crisis [5]. Climate adaptation financial innovation from the UK [8] and discussions on the insurance industry's role in supporting societal climate change adaptation [49] highlight the importance of strengthening financial resilience. Furthermore, Southeast Asian countries are expanding measures to strengthen energy infrastructure resilience in preparation for climate change impacts [78], and an analysis has suggested that extreme weather has led humanity towards a longevity economy that protects health alongside carbon neutrality [18]. Through various educational and communication activities, such as the 'Climate Kids' program [6, 63, 77], efforts to strengthen climate resilience across all age groups are spreading.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the severity of the climate crisis, alongside the multifaceted global efforts underway to address it. Only sustained attention and participation will drive stronger climate action. This concludes the climate briefing for October 5, 2026.
